gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the panel in the ALLPOWERS P1800 600 W kit (SP039) draws 13.63 A at its maximum power point. That is above the P1800's 13 A solar-input limit (we have this limit only from a search snippet; the page still needs opening), so the kit should top out near 572 W at rated output, not 600 W. A second SP039 would gain nothing: two in series make 105.6 V open-circuit, over the 60 V input range, and two in parallel hit the same 13 A limit.
standout_why: I opened StormWatts (cited). It explains clipping, series versus parallel wiring, and input-current limits in general, and gives input V/A for the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (12–60 V, 20 A, 1,000 W) and the Anker C1000 Gen 2 (600 W, 60 V max). It says nothing about the ALLPOWERS P1800 or the SP039 panel, or the BLUETTI Elite 100 mini's 350 W solar limit. I could not open the other cited pages: theoutageready.com and unpluggedwatts.com failed with a self-signed certificate error, and solargenreview.com returned HTTP 429. So 'new' is judged against StormWatts and the result titles only. The score falls to 1 if those pages turn out to cover it.
decides: This confirms the choice rather than changing it. The P1800 + 600 W kit is still the quickest-to-refill ~1 kWh kit we link: 1,024 Wh ÷ about 572 W is about 1.8 h of full sun at rated output, against 1,024 ÷ 600 = 1.7 h if nothing were clipped, so the clipping costs about 5%. The page should still say that this kit is the most solar the P1800 can use, so adding panels later does nothing. The opposite case is the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2, which takes 1,000 W at 12–60 V and 20 A (StormWatts), leaving about 650–900 W of room above its 100/200/350 W kits. The Elite 100 mini's 350 W kit already uses the station's whole 350 W solar input. The mini's 700 W total AC limit also means its kits cannot run the 1,500 W or larger appliances that both ChatGPT answers treat as the minimum.

findings.note: The manual also says 'Always check the power station's solar input voltage parameters and connect panels within the specified range.' Arithmetic: two in series = 105.6 V open-circuit, which is over a 60 V input range.

findings.note: Read through storecheck.py's search of iallpowers.com (product JSON text). Arithmetic: if the input is limited to 13 A, the SP039 at its Vmp gives 13 A × 44 V = 572 W, so the current limit sets the ceiling, not the 650 W one. The 13 A figure itself is not sourced; see unsourced.
